can be considered an official ruling. I was under the impression that
official rulings were to be in the form of quarterly updates after the
rules team (made up of more than just LSJ) had a chance to discuss it,
rather than "off the cuff" commentary. If this is how rulings are going
to come down in the future, I sure as hell will not advocate that the
NJL will combine with the VEKN for the forseeable future. This is
exactly the reason that the NJL split off in the first place.

First off, Scoot, I'd like to apologize for being so adversarial in my
early posting. I went a tad overboard. Of course, me being a hot
headed asshole from time to time is nothing new. Blame it on me being
officially "over 30" tomorrow. *wry grin*

That said, let me try to address my concerns in a more diplomatic
and constructive manner.

>> Noal McDonald wrote:
>> Unless LSJ has become a Rules Team of one person, I don't see
>> how this can be considered an official ruling.

LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
> All "answers" from the Net.Rep are official. Nothing new there.

However, they shouldn't be implied to be "final" until the rules team
has a chance to discuss and approve said answers. Towards that, it
would probably be a good idea to state your decision in a separate
post entitled to the effect of "LSJ Temp Ruling 24-MAR-2000", rather
than just in a reply. This would make it easier to reference in Deja
(and other newsgroup readers) and it would also make it clear that the
issue may change in the near future (say someone makes a compelling
argument for a contrary interpretation).

>> If this is how rulings are going to come down in the future,
>> I sure [...] will not advocate that the NJL will combine with

>> the VEKN for the forseeable future. This is exactly the reason

>> that the NJL split off in the first place.
>

> Nice.

As I stated earlier, my concern was that you would issue rulings that
were considered final, rather than pending, at irregular intervals. As
this puts extra strain on the ability for tournament moderators to keep
up with changes as evidenced on a larger scale by the aftermath of the
6/23 and 7/7 rulings, this is an issue that I would really rather not
see get stirred up again.

> As stated previously, the card text is contradictory.

It's not really as contradictory as you seem to think it is. For
example, do you pay the 1 pool for Short Term Investment _when_
(meaning "as") the card is played or _before_ the card is played?
Clearly, the pool is not paid afterwards.

> The appropriate solution to that is to issue errata resolving
> the problem.

No, the appropriate solution IMO is to state "pending final decision by
the rules team, the appropriate interpretation is..." Meaning that
only clarifications should be issued until you've had a chance to
discuss the matter with your rules team.

> The alternative is to say "there is no official
> answer - make it up as you go if the question regarding this
> ambiguity comes up in a tournament", which is not acceptable.

However, if the issue comes up first at a tournament rather than on the
newsgroup, that's exactly what does happen. The only alternative is to
go over every single card, one at a time, with your rules team and
decide whether the wording is clear enough and whether there are any
overtly unbalancing effects.

> As with such non-obvious errata and rulings that had to be issued
> off-the-cuff before, the matter will be placed before the RT for
> confirmation.

As I said above, this should be made more clear in the future.

> Or does the NJL prefer to shift the off-the-cuff ruling
> responsibility to the judges in the middle of a tournament?

If a judge in a tournament, NJL or VEKN, comes across an issue that
hasn't come up before that's exactly what they have to do. That's why
judges are given authority to make binding rules decisions during a
tournament.

OTOH, since our judges are usually members of our rules team and, in
most cases, at least three rules team members are present at
tournaments, we can usually get at least temporary consensus on an
issue. Of course, that's the strength of a smaller group. Since your
rules team is likely a bit more spread out geographically, that's much
more difficult for you to arrange.

Again, I apologize for earlier. I'm not trying to burn bridges in the
community. I just want to make sure it's being served as best as
possible...esp. in light of the recent changing of hands.

While completely accurate, I'm certain, that wasn't the perception at
the time for those people that weren't in the loop for whatever
reason. As far as I recall (and my memory can be faulty here), it
wasn't properly communicated that LSJ was the front man of a rules
team until after the outcry had already started.

Most people I talked to were aware only that LSJ had been given final
authority and that nobody from the design team was willing to answer
any further questions regarding the game. It was believed by those
same people that he was a lone gunman so to speak. I won't name names,
but I can recall specific concerns in here, as well on the Michigan
Jyhad mailing list, that LSJ had no rules team and was the first and
last authority on card rulings.

Either way, LSJ was the only visible person of an otherwise amorphous,
anonymous rules team. When this was finally known, the lack of straight
answers when questions were asked regarding the basis for and process
by which a person joined the rules team only further added to the
already existing rumors. People do tend to get suspicious of the man
behind the curtain when they stand in the antechamber of the wizard of
the Emerald City.

The point I'm coming to is that a large part of what transpired in the
aftermath of the 7/7 rulings, including the NJL, was a direct result of
suspicions and rumors that eroded the trust that LSJ otherwise would
have enjoyed after being given the reins by the design team. After
all, people generally dislike drastic change. When that change isn't
explained to their satisfaction, they also generally distrust or fear
it as well.

And that, James, is why things are the way they are in the VTES
community. We can work to build those bridges again, but tempers are
going to flare from time to time (esp. mine if I post before my morning
coffee...just don't take it too seriously) and we'll just have to be
forgiving and willing to compromise on both sides.

points?

i think there's a bit of revisionist history going on here. The NJL
weren't the only people who were hacked off with the 7/7 rulings, and
anyone who wants a full list of the complacently slow-minded minions of
chaos and entropy needs only to wade through about eight virtual tons of
diatribe to get it [apart from card-carrying members of the NJL, me and
Sorrow were pretty vocal about it IIRC]. It always seemed to me that our
strongest argument was against the principle of amending the texts of
cards, because it meant that players without net access just had to take
the word of players who did have net access that the card did what they
said it did. i understood why people wanted RtI and the Tomb kneecapped.
i just thought that there was a price to pay, which they hadn't thought
over sufficiently.

Now i think that this is all water under the bridge. Having explained why
i thought card-fixes were such a bad idea, i never really thought about
splitting or inciting others to split, largely because i didn't think
there were enough of us locally to get away with it. And the game is
doing just fine, and is going to be revitalised under White Wolf's benign
rulership. Texts will once again be readable as such, which will restore
an important measure of independence to the average player. i'm really
glad that in this new atmosphere the NJL may rejoin the fold, which they
can do with honour COMPLETELY intact having, in my view, provided an
important source of opposition to what i still think was a political
misjudgement by the rules team.
